title: Was the Moon Landing Fake? The Evidence vs. The Conspiracy
snippet: Every line of independently verifiable evidence — physical samples, laser reflectors, orbital photography, international tracking data, and fifty years of scientific study — confirms that the Apollo Moon landings were real. The hoax theory rests on misunderstandings of optics and physics, originated with a non-scientist, and has never produced a single piece of positive evidence. The probability that the Moon landings were faked is effectively zero. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), launched in 2009, photographed all six Apollo landing sites and captured images of the descent stages, equipment, and even astronaut footpaths still visible on the surface. Retroreflector laser ranging arrays were placed on the lunar surface during Apollo 11, 14, and 15. Scientists worldwide — including observatories in France, Japan, and the McDonald Observatory in Texas — have been bouncing laser beams off these reflectors since 1969 and continue to do so today.

stance_why: Addresses the qualification's escape hatch (reflectors could have been placed robotically): three large arrays were in place and being laser-ranged within days of the crewed missions, with no documented robotic missions capable of the placements.
